bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Product quality and regulatory compliance failure — Identified as the company's first material issue. Product quality is critical to regulatory compliance, patient safety, supply continuity and customer trust; quality failures or non-compliance may result in regulatory actions, product recalls, supply disruptions and loss of customer trust. As a CDMO operating five facilities across USFDA, EMA, Health Canada, MHRA and WHO regimes, the company underwent 49 regulatory inspections and customer audits in FY26, so inspection outcomes are a continuing structural exposure.
- Customer and revenue concentration in a relationship-driven CDMO model — The CDMO business model is described as relationship-driven, requiring deep customer engagement and reliable execution across multiple stages of development and manufacturing, making strong customer partnerships critical to business growth. Concentration is visible in the disclosures: 50+ of the 80+ global customers account for two or more projects, and sales to related parties were 29.12% of total sales in FY26 (54.14% in FY25).
- Dependence on customer regulatory approval timing — FY26 revenue declined and the anticipated commercialisation cycle was deferred because semaglutide approvals in Canada were delayed beyond the company's FY26 timeline. Because revenue conversion depends on third-party approval events outside the company's control, timing slippage translates directly into revenue and margin deferral, as it did in FY26.
- Supply chain disruption and single-source dependency — Identified as a material issue: reliable access to raw materials, critical inputs and specialised suppliers is essential for manufacturing continuity, product quality and on-time delivery, and supply chains may be affected by supplier constraints, geopolitical developments, logistics constraints and regulatory changes. Management explicitly notes that single-source dependencies, long lead times and minimal buffers carry structural vulnerabilities, and that for a CDMO with patient-critical products the cost of disruption is rarely incremental.
- Cybersecurity breach and loss of customer intellectual property — Identified as a material issue and rated risk-only. The company is entrusted with proprietary customer assets including formulations, cell lines, analytical methods, regulatory dossiers and development data; cybersecurity incidents or data breaches may affect intellectual property, operations, customer trust and business continuity. Mitigation rests on ISO 27001 and ISO 27701-certified systems, role-based access controls, encryption and continuous monitoring.
- Execution and ramp-up risk on the capacity expansion programme — The company is mid-way through a four-year, roughly US$100 million capex programme with about 80% committed, funded through internal accruals and borrowings, and is carrying an elevated cost base while the DDC facility ramps. FY26 EBITDA fell 35% partly on that elevated cost base, and the second cartridge line is still in qualification with commercialisation only expected in Q2FY27, so the FY28 revenue and margin guidance depends on converting this capacity into commercial volumes on schedule.
- Elevated working capital and leverage during the commercial ramp — Working capital rose materially in FY26 as the company invested in operational readiness for semaglutide commercial launches; debtors turnover fell to 2.4x from 5.5x, inventory turnover to 1.5x from 5.1x, and the debt-equity ratio rose on increased borrowings to support DDC capacity expansion. Management expects normalisation as volumes scale, but the position remains a structural exposure until that conversion occurs.
- Geographic and geopolitical concentration — All five manufacturing plants are located in Bengaluru, India with no international plants, while exports contributed 70.80% of standalone turnover. Management cites geopolitical shifts, supply chain shocks and evolving trade policy — including the US NDAA 2026 and BIOSECURE Act — as permanent features of the operating environment rather than periodic events, so a single-geography manufacturing base serving predominantly export markets is a structural concentration.
- Occupational health and safety exposure across pharmaceutical operations — Identified as a material issue: employees and contractors may be exposed to occupational hazards associated with pharmaceutical production, laboratory operations and equipment handling. Safety incidents may result in injuries, operational disruption, regulatory exposure, compensation costs and reputational impact. Managed through an EHS framework with Board-level oversight and ISO 45001-certified management systems.
- Talent attrition in a specialised, highly regulated workforce — The permanent employee turnover rate was 23% in FY26 (27% in FY25) against a workforce that grew by more than 500 professionals to over 1,600. Since the company states that the expertise and agility of its people are a key competitive advantage in an increasingly specialised industry, sustained attrition at this level is a structural constraint on executing complex programmes.

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body: OneSource Specialty Pharma is a contract development and manufacturing organisation (CDMO) serving small and large pharmaceutical companies and group purchasing organisations across regulated and emerging markets. It runs an integrated platform spanning development, analytical work, scale-up, manufacturing and commercial supply across four modalities: drug-device combinations (including GLP-1s), biologics drug substance and drug product, sterile injectables and soft gelatin capsules. The company does not market products in India directly, operating instead on behalf of customers under confidentiality obligations.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Drug-Device Combination (including GLP-1s):** Pre-filled syringes, with or without safety devices, Variable- and fixed-dose pen injectors, Dial and push injectors, Cartridges for reusable delivery systems, Pull-push delivery systems, Autoinjectors, Generic semaglutide (through partners), Tirzepatide (NCE-1 filings for customers)
- **Biologics (Drug Substance and Drug Product):** Conventional monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), Bispecific and trispecific antibodies, Fc-fusion proteins and glycoproteins, Recombinant proteins, Enzymes and peptide hormones (microbial)
- **Sterile Injectables:** Sterile liquids (Small Volume Parenterals), Lyophilised products, Dry powder injectables, Emulsions, suspensions, liposomes, nanoparticles and colloidal systems, Depot formulations, Penicillin (beta-lactam) sterile injectables
- **Oral Technologies (Soft gelatin capsules):** Immediate-release capsules, Delayed and enteric-release capsules, Chewable SoftCaps, Twist-off capsules, SMEDDS (Self-Micro Emulsifying Drug Delivery Systems)

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: OneSource is executing a four-year, approximately US$100 million capital expenditure programme focused on capacity expansion and technology upgrades, of which approximately 80% (around US$80 million) has already been committed towards infrastructure, technology integration, manufacturing equipment installation and operational readiness. The majority of the current programme is going into cartridge manufacturing capacity at the integrated DS & DP facility, in line with global demand for drug-device combination and GLP-1 delivery formats. The new cartridge filling line has been installed and is undergoing qualification activities, with commercialisation expected in Q2FY27; a second cartridge line commercialisation is flagged for Q2FY27. The programme is funded through a mix of internal accruals and borrowings, with all ongoing expansion plans fully funded through a diversified network of domestic and international banking partners, and borrowing cost declining 210 basis points year-on-year to below 9% in FY26. The company received in-principle approval for incentives under the Karnataka Industrial Policy 2025-30 for its flagship facility expansion, with a potential incentive of approximately Rs 70 crore. Beyond the current programme, the company targets an additional 5 KL of microbial capacity (on 1 KL installed) and an additional 4 KL of mammalian capacity (on 4 KL installed) for biologics, and is progressing capability expansion in sterile fill-finish across high-value formats including lyophilised products and high-viscosity formulations. The platform has been built on more than US$250 million of cumulative investment across drug-device combinations, biologics, sterile injectables and oral technologies. The company operates five state-of-the-art facilities and completed 49 regulatory inspections and customer audits in FY26, including USFDA and EMA inspections.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management expects revenues across platforms to scale significantly as it enters FY27, supported by DDC commercialisation, new customer additions, new product launches and sustained capability expansion
- The FY26 revenue shortfall was attributed to delayed semaglutide approvals in Canada which deferred a portion of the anticipated commercialisation cycle beyond FY26; management characterises this as a deferment, not a loss of opportunity, with the pipeline intact and partners committed
- FY26 EBITDA decline reflected a high MSA base in the prior year and an elevated cost base as the DDC facility ramped up, alongside continued investment in DDC scale-up, talent expansion and operational strengthening
- As commercial volumes scale, management expects improving operating leverage, stronger return metrics and better cash generation
- Elevated working capital reflects preparation for a significant commercial ramp-up, particularly for semaglutide commercial launches, and is expected to normalise as commercial volumes scale, translating into stronger cash generation and improved returns on capital employed
- Five notches of credit rating upgrade since listing reduced borrowing costs by over 200 basis points to below 9%, improving capital efficiency; all ongoing expansion plans are fully funded through a diversified network of domestic and international banking partners
- In-principle approval for incentives under the Karnataka Industrial Policy 2025-30 for the flagship facility expansion, with a potential incentive of around Rs 70 crore, improves the returns profile of the expansion
- The global CDMO market for drug-device combinations including GLP-1 therapies is expected to grow at a CAGR of over 20%, driven by adoption of autoinjectors and cartridge-based platforms and the rapid expansion of GLP-1 therapies for obesity and metabolic disorders
- The biologics CDMO market for drug substance and drug product is expected to grow at a CAGR of around 14% over the medium term, supported by rising R&D investment, biosimilar adoption as leading biologics lose exclusivity, and India emerging as a biologics hub
- The global softgel capsules market is expected to grow at a CAGR of around 9% over the medium term, supported by supply constraints in pharmaceutical-grade softgels, high technical skill requirements and growing preference for patient-friendly dosage forms
- The global sterile fill-finish CDMO market is expected to grow at a CAGR of around 5% over the medium term, supported by continued loss of exclusivity, ageing manufacturing infrastructure in mature markets and cost optimisation
- Supply chain diversification driven by changing trade dynamics, localisation initiatives and policy measures such as the proposed US BIOSECURE Act is encouraging customers to diversify manufacturing and sourcing, creating opportunities for CDMOs with scalable infrastructure and strong quality systems
- Pharmaceutical companies are shifting from transactional outsourcing to integrated, long-term CDMO partnerships spanning development, manufacturing and commercialisation, consolidating supplier networks toward end-to-end providers
- Patent expiry of leading GLP-1 therapies such as semaglutide is increasing affordability and access in price-sensitive markets, driving higher treatment volumes and demand for peptide manufacturing, injectable drug delivery systems and sterile manufacturing capabilities
- 80+ global customers, with 50+ customers running two or more projects or products; management describes long-term commitments and repeat business wins as validation of the strategy
- Biologics opportunity funnel expanded nearly 4x over FY25, supported by the addition of a European biosimilar partner, a major US biosimilar customer and a second project from a leading global animal health company
- 50+ DDC projects across 12 device platforms; 140+ tech transfer batches completed in a trailing 15-month period
- First and only CDMO to have received four semaglutide approvals across G7 markets, with all generic semaglutide approvals across the G7 secured through its partners; multiple Tirzepatide NCE-1 filings completed for customers
- Across the injectables and softgel businesses, multiple licensing and CDMO agreements were signed, new products launched and the customer base and specialty product portfolio expanded
- Management cites a growing commercial pipeline with programmes approaching commercialisation, and recent semaglutide approvals and product launches across regulated and emerging markets as providing strong visibility into future growth

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management expects revenues across platforms to scale significantly as it enters FY27, supported by DDC commercialisation, new customer additions, new product launches and sustained capability expansion
- The FY26 revenue shortfall was attributed to delayed semaglutide approvals in Canada which deferred a portion of the anticipated commercialisation cycle beyond FY26; management characterises this as a deferment, not a loss of opportunity, with the pipeline intact and partners committed
- FY26 EBITDA decline reflected a high MSA base in the prior year and an elevated cost base as the DDC facility ramped up, alongside continued investment in DDC scale-up, talent expansion and operational strengthening
- As commercial volumes scale, management expects improving operating leverage, stronger return metrics and better cash generation
- Elevated working capital reflects preparation for a significant commercial ramp-up, particularly for semaglutide commercial launches, and is expected to normalise as commercial volumes scale, translating into stronger cash generation and improved returns on capital employed
- Five notches of credit rating upgrade since listing reduced borrowing costs by over 200 basis points to below 9%, improving capital efficiency; all ongoing expansion plans are fully funded through a diversified network of domestic and international banking partners
- In-principle approval for incentives under the Karnataka Industrial Policy 2025-30 for the flagship facility expansion, with a potential incentive of around Rs 70 crore, improves the returns profile of the expansion
- The global CDMO market for drug-device combinations including GLP-1 therapies is expected to grow at a CAGR of over 20%, driven by adoption of autoinjectors and cartridge-based platforms and the rapid expansion of GLP-1 therapies for obesity and metabolic disorders
- The biologics CDMO market for drug substance and drug product is expected to grow at a CAGR of around 14% over the medium term, supported by rising R&D investment, biosimilar adoption as leading biologics lose exclusivity, and India emerging as a biologics hub
- The global softgel capsules market is expected to grow at a CAGR of around 9% over the medium term, supported by supply constraints in pharmaceutical-grade softgels, high technical skill requirements and growing preference for patient-friendly dosage forms
- The global sterile fill-finish CDMO market is expected to grow at a CAGR of around 5% over the medium term, supported by continued loss of exclusivity, ageing manufacturing infrastructure in mature markets and cost optimisation
- Supply chain diversification driven by changing trade dynamics, localisation initiatives and policy measures such as the proposed US BIOSECURE Act is encouraging customers to diversify manufacturing and sourcing, creating opportunities for CDMOs with scalable infrastructure and strong quality systems
- Pharmaceutical companies are shifting from transactional outsourcing to integrated, long-term CDMO partnerships spanning development, manufacturing and commercialisation, consolidating supplier networks toward end-to-end providers
- Patent expiry of leading GLP-1 therapies such as semaglutide is increasing affordability and access in price-sensitive markets, driving higher treatment volumes and demand for peptide manufacturing, injectable drug delivery systems and sterile manufacturing capabilities
- 80+ global customers, with 50+ customers running two or more projects or products; management describes long-term commitments and repeat business wins as validation of the strategy
- Biologics opportunity funnel expanded nearly 4x over FY25, supported by the addition of a European biosimilar partner, a major US biosimilar customer and a second project from a leading global animal health company
- 50+ DDC projects across 12 device platforms; 140+ tech transfer batches completed in a trailing 15-month period
- First and only CDMO to have received four semaglutide approvals across G7 markets, with all generic semaglutide approvals across the G7 secured through its partners; multiple Tirzepatide NCE-1 filings completed for customers
- Across the injectables and softgel businesses, multiple licensing and CDMO agreements were signed, new products launched and the customer base and specialty product portfolio expanded
- Management cites a growing commercial pipeline with programmes approaching commercialisation, and recent semaglutide approvals and product launches across regulated and emerging markets as providing strong visibility into future growth

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: OneSource is executing a four-year, approximately US$100 million capital expenditure programme focused on capacity expansion and technology upgrades, of which approximately 80% (around US$80 million) has already been committed towards infrastructure, technology integration, manufacturing equipment installation and operational readiness. The majority of the current programme is going into cartridge manufacturing capacity at the integrated DS & DP facility, in line with global demand for drug-device combination and GLP-1 delivery formats. The new cartridge filling line has been installed and is undergoing qualification activities, with commercialisation expected in Q2FY27; a second cartridge line commercialisation is flagged for Q2FY27. The programme is funded through a mix of internal accruals and borrowings, with all ongoing expansion plans fully funded through a diversified network of domestic and international banking partners, and borrowing cost declining 210 basis points year-on-year to below 9% in FY26. The company received in-principle approval for incentives under the Karnataka Industrial Policy 2025-30 for its flagship facility expansion, with a potential incentive of approximately Rs 70 crore. Beyond the current programme, the company targets an additional 5 KL of microbial capacity (on 1 KL installed) and an additional 4 KL of mammalian capacity (on 4 KL installed) for biologics, and is progressing capability expansion in sterile fill-finish across high-value formats including lyophilised products and high-viscosity formulations. The platform has been built on more than US$250 million of cumulative investment across drug-device combinations, biologics, sterile injectables and oral technologies. The company operates five state-of-the-art facilities and completed 49 regulatory inspections and customer audits in FY26, including USFDA and EMA inspections.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- One of the few sites globally to offer integrated drug substance and drug product manufacturing from the same site, reducing technology transfer complexity for customers

- One of the few USFDA-approved penicillin manufacturing facilities globally and a Top 5 penicillin supplier to the US in molecules supplied there; penicillin requires dedicated, segregated facilities, which raises the barrier to entry
- Top 5 global softgel capacity with 2.4 billion installed softgel capacity and 30+ years of development and manufacturing experience
- Multi-modality platform spanning DDC, biologics, sterile injectables and oral technologies, letting customers consolidate increasingly complex programmes with a single partner
- Regulatory and quality track record: 200+ successful audits, 49 regulatory inspections and customer audits completed in FY26 including USFDA and EMA, and zero Class I product recalls in the last four years
- Broad device expertise across 12 device platforms with 50+ DDC projects and 140+ tech transfer batches completed in a trailing 15-month period
- Sticky, expanding customer relationships: 80+ global customers, with 50+ customers running two or more projects/products
- Platform built on more than US$250 million of investment across DDCs, biologics, sterile injectables and oral technologies
- Five notches of credit rating upgrades since listing in January 2025, reaching the A category with a Positive outlook, reducing borrowing cost by over 200 basis points to below 9%
